report.summary: Reviewed chunk 3 of docrefs.py: FixVerdict dataclass, iter_doc_files, _strip_code_blocks, extract_references, _EXCLUDED_DIRS, and _suffix_index.
risks: _suffix_index | medium | The docstring claims 370 of 374 skipped references were relative, but the code does not show this measurement or any logic that uses it; this claim is uncheckable in this chunk.

_EXCLUDED_DIRS | low | The comment says 'build/ is the killer' but the code only excludes the directory name; no check is made for a 'build' directory at any depth. This is consistent with the code but the comment may be misleading if the intent was to exclude only a top-level 'build'.

handoff.purpose: Define FixVerdict, file iteration, code block stripping, reference extraction, excluded dirs, and suffix index.

symbols.note: Frozen dataclass with fields ok, verdict, detail, resolving_before, resolving_after, and to_dict method.

symbols.note: Returns sorted tuple of Paths matching DOC_GLOBS patterns under repo_root.

claims.text: ``ok`` is False for ``evidence_destroyed`` no matter what else happened.
claims.why: The code does not implement any logic that sets ok based on verdict; the claim is about external usage not present.

claims.text: Every prose file in the corpus, sorted, deduplicated.
claims.why: The function returns tuple(sorted(set(found))) after globbing patterns in DOC_GLOBS.

claims.text: Two kinds of code are dropped: fenced blocks, and lines indented four or more spaces that are not list continuations.
claims.why: The code explicitly handles fenced blocks (lines matching _FENCE and inside fence) and indented lines (line[:4]=='    ' and not _LIST_MARKER.match(stripped)).

claims.text: The dropped COUNT is returned so "not checked" is reported rather than implied.
claims.why: The function returns (prose, dropped) where dropped is an int count of dropped lines.

claims.text: Everything returned is UNRESOLVED -- shape only. :func:`resolve_reference` decides what is true.
claims.why: The function returns references with doc_path, line, raw; no resolution logic is present; resolve_reference is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: A trailing call suffix is how prose names a function; it is not part of the name.
claims.why: Code: probe = raw[:-2].strip() if raw.endswith('()') else raw.

claims.text: build/ is the killer: it holds a COPY of daedalus/, so without this every basename in the repo is ambiguous and suffix resolution silently resolves nothing at all.
claims.why: The code only excludes a directory named 'build' (among others); the claim about 'COPY of daedalus/' and ambiguity is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Measured: 370 of 374 skipped references were relative like this, so a root-anchored resolver was declining to check the overwhelming majority of the corpus and reporting a confident zero.
claims.why: No measurement or reference to such data appears in this chunk; the claim is about external analysis.

claims.text: A suffix resolves ONLY when exactly one module ends with it. Ambiguity is the absent-module case: two files named index.py mean this module cannot tell which one the sentence is about, and guessing would manufacture a finding against a file the author never mentioned.
claims.why: The code shown builds a dict mapping suffix to list of paths, but does not show the resolution logic that enforces exactly one match.
